entries.def:
εἰμί, 
with various uses and significations, like the English verb to be. 
__I. As substantive verb. 
__1. Of persons and things, to be, exist: Act.17.28, Jhn.1.1; 8.58; 17.5, al; ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν (for past ptcp.), Rev.1.4, 8; 4.8; 11.17; 16.5 (see Swete, Ap., 5; M, Pr., 228); τὰ (μὴ) ὄντα, Rom.4.17, 1Co.1.28. 
__2. Of times, events, etc., to be, happen, take place: Mat.24.3, Mrk.14.2; 15.42, Luk.21.23, Jhn.4.6, 23;…

ἔσ-οπτρον, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX: Wis.7.26, Sir.12.11 * ;] 
a mirror: 1Co.13.12, Jas.1.23.†
(AS)

ἑσπέρα, -ας, ἡ
(prop, fem, of ἕσπερος), [in LXX chiefly for עָרַב ;] 
__(a) (sc. ὥρα), evening: Luk.24.29, Act.4.3; 20.15; 28.23; 
__(b) (so. χώρα), the west.†
(AS)

Ἑσρώμ 
(Ἑσρών, Lk, l.with; Rec. Ἑσρ-), ὁ (Heb. חֶצְרוֹן, Gen.46.12, Num.26.21, 1Ch.25.1-31, al.), [in LXX both forms, ut supr. (cf. ICC, on Mt, l.with; WH, § 408) ;] 
Esrom (AV), Hezron (RV), an ancestor of Jesus: Mat.13.1-58, Luk.3.35.†
(AS)

ἐσχάτως 
adv., 
extremely, utterly; ἐ. ἔχειν (= Lat. in extremis esse), only in late writers (cf. ἐν ἐσχάτοις εἶναι, FlJ, Ant., ix, 8, 6), to be at the point of death: Mrk.5.28.†
(AS)
